title: Fix the ledger entry check
prompt: Every ledger entry gets a check label, but entries with no type, amount or currency come out `ok`, and so do entries of 0.00. Fix `solve(ledger_entries)`.
rules: Check in this order and use the first problem found: `no transfer` (`transfer_id` missing), `bad type` (`entry_type` missing or not `debit` or `credit`), `bad amount` (`amount` missing or not more than 0), `bad currency` (`currency` missing or not `USD`, `EUR` or `GBP`).
An entry with none of these problems gets `ok`.
Return `entry_id` and `check`, in that order, for every entry.
hints: Follow an entry with a missing `entry_type` through the starter: `~F.col("entry_type").isin(...)` is NULL, not true, so that `when` doesn't match.
Add `F.col(...).isNull() |` in front of each rule that can meet a missing value.
explanation: A rule on a missing value is NULL, and a `when` only fires on true, so an entry with no type, amount or currency falls past every check and lands in `otherwise("ok")`. Each rule needs its missing case spelled out: `.when(F.col("entry_type").isNull() | ~F.col("entry_type").isin("debit", "credit"), "bad type")`, `.when(F.col("amount").isNull() | (F.col("amount") <= 0), "bad amount")` and `.when(F.col("currency").isNull() | ~F.col("currency").isin("USD", "EUR", "GBP"), "bad currency")`. The second bug is `< 0`: the rule says an amount must be more than 0, so 0.00 is bad too, and the test is `<= 0`. The `transfer_id` rule was already right, because `isNull()` is never NULL itself.
